newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX ends near 4,100 at new record high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX ends near 4,100 at new record high.

text.p: Hungarian stocks rallied in brisk trading on Friday, not only adding to recent peaks but also breaking the 4,000-point level for the first time ever.
The BUX index finished at 4,096.52 points, up 134.36 or 3.39 percent. A number of leading stocks hit new record highs.
"The rise of the index speaks for itself," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities.
"I would say the reason behind the rally is that Moody's upgrading urged everybody to buy more stocks on the market which enjoys enormous investor confidence."
Moody's said on Thursday that it had upgraded the sovereign ceiling for foreign currency debt of Hungary to Baa3 from Ba1.

"The market's positive mood is beyond doubt and the upgrade was just one more catalyst," one trader said. "The market would have risen even without the upgrade -- there are only a few trading days left this year and investors apparently want to boost their portfolios."
Most market participants are apparently shrugging off warnings by the more cautious that some stocks are already overvalued, Lencs said.
While the market was rallying the bourse suspended trading in hotel firm Eravis and dairy firm Hajdutej for the day.
The BSE suspended Eravis because the company had not informed the bourse that as leader of a consortium it had acquired a 50 percent stake in Hunguest Hotels Rt.
Newspaper reports on the subject were contradictory and they could influence investors in their decisions, it said.
Hajdutej was suspended after a newspaper report said Dutch dairy firm Friesland Dairy Foods Holding N.V. planned to take over another Dutch dairy company Nutricia 's stake in Hajdutej Rt.
Nutricia currently holds 79.6 percent of Hajdutej and plans to boost this to 96.7 percent by the end of the year, the report added.
"Disregarding whether it is true or not, the newspaper's information could influence investors in their invesment decisions," the bourse statement said.
